What SANKET keeps, and how to delete it

1. SANKET reads your signal every second and works out how fast it is falling.

2. When the chance of losing signal in the next 10 seconds passes 70%, it saves your downloads at once.

3. If a nearby tower stays strong, it's only a handover, so SANKET stays quiet.

4. It remembers places where you lost signal before, and notices lifts with the barometer (or the motion sensor, on phones without one), so it can act even earlier.

When the signal comes back, downloads continue from where they stopped.

SANKET watches your phone's signal so it can save your downloads before the signal drops.

What it reads: the signal of each SIM, whether the internet works, air pressure or the phone's movement (to notice lifts) and your location while protection runs.

Where it goes: nowhere. Everything stays on this phone, encrypted.

What it keeps: places where you lost signal, rounded to about 11 m, and a safety log for 30 days.

Android will ask about phone calls. SANKET only uses that permission to see your SIM cards; it never makes, reads or records calls.

You can delete everything at any time under Privacy.
No places yet. SANKET remembers a place after it loses signal there on two separate visits.
For example: use gate 3, lift B has no signal
Nothing logged yet. Signal losses longer than 10 seconds appear here, with the time and place. The demo is not logged.
It lists the times and rounded places where your phone lost signal. Share it only with people you trust.

SANKET watches your phone's signal so it can save your downloads before the signal drops.

What it reads: the signal of each SIM, whether the internet works, air pressure or the phone's movement (to notice lifts) and your location while protection runs.

Where it goes: nowhere. Everything stays on this phone, encrypted with a key that can't leave the phone. Apart from the downloads you start, SANKET sends nothing to any server.

What it keeps: places where you lost signal (rounded to about 11 m and forgotten after some weeks without new losses) and a safety log for 30 days.
This deletes all places, notes, the safety log and unfinished downloads from this phone. It can\'t be undone.
All SANKET data on this phone was deleted.
Some phones stop apps in the background to save battery, which also stops protection. Here is where to allow SANKET on your phone.
Settings, Apps, SANKET: turn on Autostart, then set Battery saver to No restrictions.
Settings, Apps, SANKET, Battery: choose Unrestricted. Also check that SANKET isn\'t in Sleeping apps under Battery, Background usage limits.
Settings, Apps, SANKET, Battery usage: allow background activity, and auto launch if you see it.
Settings, Battery, Background power consumption management: set SANKET to Allow.
Settings, Apps, SANKET, Battery: choose Unrestricted or Don\'t optimise.
The exact names differ a little between phone models.
